dedupe_keys.name: recommendation itu r p 833 attenuation in vegetation models and measured data

description: Recommendation ITU-R P.833 is the international reference for how trees and other vegetation weaken radio signals. It sets out models for the extra loss when a path passes through woodland, a single tree or a row of trees, or runs along the top of a forest canopy, for frequencies from 30 MHz to 100 GHz, with specific attenuation per metre and a limit on total loss set by other propagation mechanisms. It also includes collated measurement data from studies in several countries: for example, measurements through single trees show an average reduction of about 20 dB per tree with frequent fades of up to 50 dB, along with data on fade dynamics caused by wind and on delay spread. The recommendation has been revised many times; version 10 dates from September 2021. Coverage: generic models with measurements from multiple countries and vegetation types. Format and access: PDF recommendation free from the ITU website. Caveats: models are empirical and need local vegetation parameters; measured data are summarised in tables and figures, not supplied as raw files; seasonal leaf state changes results. Simulation uses: propagation loss for mobile and fixed wireless coverage in wooded and suburban areas, sensitivity of links to vegetation growth or loss after storms and fires, and calibration of planning tools. Related records: the NTIA propagation models and Signal Server compute path loss, and the Vienna drive-test data give urban measurements.
